# Regional repair-network decision, version 2 (synthetic)

Produce an executable Go analysis and a source-linked Markdown recommendation from the frozen data room. This is a synthetic four-facility operation, not evidence of market demand. The decision cutoff is `2026-07-15T23:59:59Z`; the analysis period is the four calendar months March–June 2026. Read only the supplied files and register their source IDs and SHA-256 bytes; include `manifest-v2` for `manifest.json` plus the eight source IDs listed within it. `O-analysis` owns `analysis.go`, `metrics.json`, and `sources.json`; `O-document` depends on that unit and owns `memo.md`. `analysis.go` must run as `go run analysis.go -data <directory> -out <metrics path>` in an isolated copy, and the committed metric file must equal its generated output. Keep currency in integer cents and duration in integer minutes. No unrestricted web research, external accounts, live notifications, or binary office authoring are part of this task.

## Reconcile records before aggregating

`orders.json` has one immutable order per `order_id`, including created time, priority, assigned facility and warranty flag. `events_initial.json` and `events_corrections.json` together form one append-only event stream. For each order, choose the event with greatest `recorded_at` at or before cutoff; break exact-time ties by larger integer `revision`, then lexicographically larger `event_id`. A chosen event fully replaces status, completion time, work minutes, charge and parts. Ignore events recorded after cutoff even if their completion time is earlier. Reject duplicate event IDs or an event referring to an unknown order. Report total, selected, future-ignored, corrected (chosen revision > 1), cancelled and completed counts. Cancelled orders remain in reconciliation counts and are excluded from operating metrics. `open` and `scheduled` chosen statuses count toward backlog. A nonempty warranty job with known zero charge remains a completed/SLA-eligible job. `null` is unknown, numeric zero is known zero; never silently impute unknown as zero. All timestamps are UTC RFC3339. The frozen room contains late corrections, status reversals, tied revisions and missing fields. Keep source grain explicit.

## SLA, parts, labor and capacity

Select the policy with greatest `effective_at <= order.created_at` for that priority; tie by larger revision. A completed noncancelled job with a completion timestamp is SLA-eligible. Completion at or before creation plus target hours is on time. Report eligible, on-time and late counts, attainment as a decimal string rounded half-up to four places (null for zero denominator), known credit cents and unknown-credit job count. For each late job with known charge, calculate `charge_cents * credit_bps / 10000`, round half-up to integer cents **per job**, then sum. A zero-charge late warranty job contributes known zero; a missing charge increments unknown-credit jobs. Do not select the numerically largest policy target or credit rate instead of the effective revision.

Each selected completed event has a `parts` array. For each line with positive known quantity, select the matching supplier rate with greatest `effective_at <= completed_at`, tie by revision, calculate quantity × unit cents, then sum across lines and jobs. A line with known zero quantity costs zero without needing a rate. A null quantity or positive quantity without an effective rate is unknown; report unknown-part line count and the number of distinct jobs containing one. Do not use a product of aggregate quantities and prices. For labor, select the `capacity.json` row by assigned facility and completion month. Known work minutes × loaded hourly cents / 60 is rounded half-up **per completed job** before summing. Report known labor cents and unknown-labor job count. Missing work minutes do not become free labor. The frozen completed jobs all fall within the four-month analysis period.

`capacity.json` has one row per facility and month with available minutes and loaded hourly cents. Report each row's available minutes and known used minutes from selected completed jobs. Missing work minutes make that site's capacity feasibility unknown rather than safely below capacity. A portfolio is capacity-feasible only if every included site/month has zero unknown-work jobs and used minutes no greater than available minutes. `shared_costs.json` gives monthly pairwise dispatch costs: add each pair once for every active pair in a portfolio, plus each active site's monthly fixed cost, over all four months. `portfolios.json` declares the options; do not invent or omit one. A portfolio covers only completed jobs originally assigned to its included sites; there is no unsupported reassignment. Report covered jobs, covered-job ratio (half-up four-place string), known variable cents (labor + parts + credits of covered jobs), four-month fixed-plus-shared cents, and their sum as a **period cost lower bound**. Unknown charges/parts/labor remain disclosed and make the lower bound uncertain. A declared option is decision-eligible only when capacity-feasible and covered-job ratio is at least the threshold in `manifest.json`. Report each option and sort a separate eligible ranking by lower-bound cost, then name.

Run two scoped sensitivities. First, raise only `relay` supplier rates whose selected rate effective date is at or after `2026-04-01T00:00:00Z` by 10%, rounding half-up **per unit** before line multiplication; report baseline and scenario known-part totals without changing labor, SLA or fixed costs. Second, reduce only west facility's June available minutes by 15%, rounding down to whole minutes, and report which declared portfolios change capacity feasibility and decision eligibility. Do not apply either scenario to unrelated records.

Output stable JSON sections `selection`, `backlog`, `sla`, `cost`, `capacity`, `portfolios`, `eligible_ranking`, and `sensitivity`, with explicit numerator/denominator/unknown counts and source register. The memo compares **all declared options** in a numeric evidence table whose rows contain JSON pointer, exact value and relevant source IDs (for example `| /backlog | 4 | orders-v2, events-initial-v2, events-corrections-v2 |`). Cover selection orders/corrected/future/cancelled/completed, backlog, SLA eligible/on-time/attainment/unknown-credit/zero-charge, known part/labor/credit and unknown part/labor counts, relay and west-June sensitivities, plus each option's covered jobs, coverage ratio, period cost lower bound, capacity feasibility and decision eligibility. Add plain-text `Recommendation: <declared option>`, `Criterion: ...` and `Uncertainty: ...` lines, an operating plan, and a risk/assumption register. A different decision-eligible recommendation is allowed when its criterion and coverage/cost/unknown-data tradeoffs are explicit; a lower-cost partial-coverage option is not automatically best. Do not claim the synthetic orders forecast demand or that omitted work transfers freely. A polished memo cannot compensate for wrong calculations or fabricated source claims.

Native read-only checks inspect file inventory, Go syntax, JSON structure and source hashes. They do not compile, execute or write Go code, open databases, run a browser or validate numeric outputs. The separate external qualifier compiles/runs Go only in a marked disposable copy under a stricter child sandbox, recomputes a private Python answer key from frozen source bytes, compares the exact returned artifact, and checks numeric/source links in the memo. Human semantic review remains necessary for recommendation quality. This version is a new subject workload; the smaller version-1 packet is retained only as oracle validation control and is never pooled with these outcomes.

external_qualification.sandbox: trusted Python verifier plus strict candidate Go child; run-local writes and loopback only

handoff: The contract and frozen data room are the complete accepted task facts for every arm.
Native checks are static only; external analysis/full scopes and independent semantic review remain separate.
O.objective: Analyze the synthetic four-facility repair network with executable Go and deliver a sourced Markdown decision memo.
permissions: Produce only declared candidate artifacts and run approved read-only native static checks; external qualification occurs in marked disposable copies.
prohibitions: No existing-project write, live notifications, unrestricted web research, memory enrollment, binary office file or undeclared artifact.

obligations.description: Required metric sections and exact source register hashes are present.
Go analysis source parses without a filesystem-writing build.

units.objective: Write a source-linked decision memo that compares all declared facility portfolios and respects the qualified analysis.

obligations.description: A memo with evidence table and public decision-record fields is present.

constraints.text:
# IncidentOps change request (synthetic)

This is a local exercise. The Go API and TypeScript dashboard in `starter/` already list incidents and ingest basic events. Keep useful behavior and implement the change below. No real notification is sent: `outbox` is a queryable local table only. Use the supplied Go/TypeScript stack. Preserve SQLite WAL mode and `synchronous=FULL`. `GET /api/health` reports the active connection's `{status:"ok",journal_mode:"wal",synchronous:2}` so durability can be checked without relying on a new connection's defaults. All timestamps are UTC RFC3339; reject malformed timestamps. Each request declares `X-Tenant` and `X-Role` (`operator` or `viewer`); blank or unknown values are rejected. A viewer may read only its tenant and cannot mutate any data. A tenant name is an opaque case-sensitive key.

## Event and incident contract

`POST /api/events` accepts `{event_id,incident_id,sequence,kind,occurred_at,severity,note}`. `kind` is `OPEN`, `ACK`, `RESOLVE`, or `REOPEN`. `sequence` is a positive integer per tenant/incident. `severity` is `P1`, `P2`, or `P3` for `OPEN` and `REOPEN`, and may be omitted otherwise. `note` is optional text. A new accepted event returns HTTP 201; exact replay of the same tenant/event ID and canonical JSON fields returns 200 and changes nothing; reuse of that ID with different content returns 409 and changes nothing. The same ID in a different tenant is independent. Invalid transitions return 422 without changing persisted state. The response identifies the current derived incident state. Events may arrive out of sequence. The authoritative state is the fold of all accepted events in ascending sequence, then event ID. Validate the *entire resulting ledger* before committing a late insertion; if the new fold contains any invalid transition, reject the insertion atomically with 422. A valid late insertion can alter history but must not regress the current state or duplicate current side effects. `OPEN` begins a new incident; `ACK` requires open; `RESOLVE` requires open or acknowledged; `REOPEN` requires resolved. `REOPEN` starts a new notification generation. Incidents are isolated by tenant. A process restart from the same database path preserves events, incidents, configuration, and outbox state.

`GET /api/incidents` returns `{items:[...]}` in descending latest-event time, then ascending incident ID. Each item includes `incident_id,status,severity,latest_at,note,sequence`, where sequence is the final folded event's sequence and lets the UI submit the next action. Latest-event time means the `occurred_at` of the final event in fold order, not the maximum timestamp among the incident's records. Optional `status`, `severity`, and `q` filters apply; `q` searches incident ID and current note case-insensitively. `GET /api/summary` returns `{total,open,acknowledged,resolved}` counts derived from the current filtered incident result set, including zero counts, never a separately maintained counter. Both endpoints honor exactly the same query filters. `GET /api/outbox` returns `{items:[{incident_id,generation,due_at,assignee,state},...]}` for only the caller tenant's fake entries, sorted by incident ID and generation. New and replayed event responses return `{incident:{incident_id,status,severity,latest_at,note,sequence},duplicate:boolean}`. Do not contact an external service.

## Escalation configuration and effects

`POST /api/policies` with `{effective_at,severity,delay_minutes}` appends a tenant policy revision. `delay_minutes` is an integer from 0 to 1440. For a generation opened at time T, use the policy of matching severity with the greatest `effective_at <= T`; if tied, the most recently accepted revision wins. A later revision may decrease the delay, so do not select by numeric maximum. If no revision is effective, use 60 minutes. `POST /api/oncall` with `{starts_at,ends_at,person}` appends a tenant handover interval (`starts_at < ends_at`). For due time D, select the overlapping interval with latest `starts_at`; if tied, latest accepted revision wins. No match yields `unassigned`. These configuration endpoints require `operator` and return 201. The outbox records one entry per incident generation with due time, assignee, and state `pending` or `cancelled`. An `ACK` or `RESOLVE` cancels obsolete pending work. Reopening creates the next generation and its own entry. A late event or configuration revision reconciles pending effects deterministically without creating duplicate rows. Existing cancelled generations stay cancelled.

## Dashboard and delivery

The dashboard uses the real API, presents incident rows and a visible `Summary` heading with filtered counts, and shows a clear error for rejected actions. Keep visible, accessible control labels `Tenant`, `Role`, `Status`, `Severity`, and `Search`, plus accessible action names `ACK`, `RESOLVE`, and `REOPEN` where those actions apply; these are user-facing affordances, not CSS or DOM selectors. A viewer can inspect but cannot trigger writes; hiding or disabling viewer write controls are both valid. Changing filters refreshes both rows and counts from the network. Buttons inside forms must not accidentally submit/reload. Provide a useful mobile layout. Supply `design.json` plus `design.md` for the first unit: document current callers, public API and schemas, persisted versus derived fields, migration and compatibility intent, state transitions, ownership, and executable contract examples. The second unit supplies implementation files, meaningful tests and a runbook. The first unit's accepted contract governs the second.

Public native acceptance is limited to well-formed source and declarative contract examples that can run read-only. Final integration acceptance separately compiles Go/TypeScript, exercises API and SQLite persistence in disposable copies, and checks browser behavior and performance over loopback. No native read-only result proves server, browser, restart, or throughput behavior.

handoff: The source contract is the complete accepted public task; all arms receive identical facts.
Native qualification covers only declared static obligations. Final build/API/browser/restart/performance and private oracle evidence are external and pending until verified.
